Urgent Care RV Repair &amp; Solar     www.UrgentCareRVRepair.com     Scott Harris   Santa Cruz, CA. &nbsp;April 15 to May 15   Newport, OR. Memorial Day to Labor Day   Tucson, AZ. Thanksgiving to April 1, 2019 Phone: (831) 588-3148  scott@urgentcarervrepair.com    Scott Harris has been a certified residential/commercial solar installer, and, since 2014, an RVST certified RV Technician. He is a full time RV’er. He has owned several motorhomes over the years, currently traveling and restoring a vintage Beaver Coach. &nbsp;This is his third year as an AM Solar factory trained dealer/installer. &nbsp;He is passionate about designing systems to allow his customers to achieve their RV travel dreams. &nbsp; Scott was a senior electronics technician at the University of California, where he designed and built electronic research equipment that has been to the North Pole, the South Pole, the bottom of oceans and up in space. &nbsp;He also ran the Apple Computer repair shop on campus, and retains his Apple certification. &nbsp;He is well known for his fine attention to detail and strong customer service ethic. He is spending Summer, 2018 on the Oregon Central Coast, and Winter 2018-2019 in Tucson, Arizona. &nbsp;He is booking ahead for solar installation projects along the way.  See his website for a more detailed itinerary.&nbsp; In his spare time he has volunteered with Power to the People, traveling to remote Nicaraguan villages to install solar in schools and medical facilities. &nbsp;He is a professionally trained musician, playing his trombone, sax, and flute and has traveled the world playing Jazz and Classical music. &nbsp;He and his wife Bonnie travel full time with their two African Grey Parrots and two dogs. &nbsp;Together they enjoy sourcing the best local foods and beverages.

Louis Mailisand, 17, from Tarpon Springs surfaces with the Cross. It was later determined that two other boys also initially surfaced with the Cross, Jared Alissandratos, 16, from Tarpon Springs and Alexi Lake, 16, from New Port Richey were also determined to have retrieved the Cross. It is the first time in the 106 year history of the Epiphany event that four boys have been honored as having retrieved the Cross.
